there are fewer circulating α4β7+ lymphocytes in old rats than in young rats, while there are fewer MAdCAM-+ endothelial cells in intestinal blood vessels in old rats than young rats.

the proportion of peripheral blood lymphocytes expressing the integrin α4 β7 is decreased in the blood of elderly rats and that the density of intestinal blood vessels with the addressin M-AdCAM-1 is decreased in elderly rats.

the proportion of α4 β7 - positive mononuclear cells is significantly greater in young adult than in aged rats, whereas there is only borderline statistical significance in the density of MAdCAM- l - positive blood vessels in the intestinal lamina of the two age groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the age-related changes in homing molecules and lymphocyte subsets that contribute to the age-related decline in intestinal mucosal immunity in the Fischer 344 rat.
the mechanisms of intestinal immunity and how they may change as a function of aging.
the identification of age-related alterations in the expression of lymphocyte homoming molecules and their endothelial cell receptors in the intestine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the elderly rats have significantly fewer peripheral blood mononucle-ar cells expressing α4β7 in comparison to young adult animals.

the age-associated decrease in the number of peripheral blood monocytes expressing the homing receptor α4β7 is not accompanied by a significant decrease in the density of the intestinal addressin MAd-CAM-1.
the expression of α4β1 in peripheral blood mononuciear cells decreases with aging, while the expression of MadCAM-1 in the intestinal lamina increases, but not to a statistically significant degree.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is no significant change in the expression of the addressin MADCAM-1 in the intestinal lamina of young and old Fischer 344 rats, whereas there is a significant decrease in the number of peripheral blood monocytes and lymphocytes expressing the α4β7 integrin.

there is an age-related decrease in the proportion of circulating lymphocytes that express the homing integrins, α4β7, which is accompanied by a concomitant decrease in the number of MAdCAM- 1-expressing blood vessels in the intestinal lamina.
the expression of α4β1 is significantly decreased with age in the blood, while the expression of MAdCAM- 1 is significantly increased in the lamina propria.

the elderly have a diminished capacity to recruit IgA immunobasts into the intestinal lamina to provide protection against enteric infectious agents.
the elderly have fewer lymphocytes that express the α4β7 integrin, and the number of intestinal blood vessels with MAddCAM-l-positive endothelium is reduced.
